note_body: Israel's leaders carry in spice and oil for the sanctuary's light, and Paul calls a congregation's practical gift an odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice wellpleasing to God. Tangible help, brought in surrendered hands, rises as fragrance.
lens_gloss: spice, balsam fragrance — worship you can smell; devotion carried into God's house by willing hands.

note_body: Genesis says we were created in God's own image, and Paul says we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works. Conviction stands on that foundation — the Spirit corrects a masterpiece, He never discards one.
lens_gloss: image, likeness — every person bears the Maker's stamp; conviction restores the image, it never erases the worth.

note_body: God writes inheritance law so no family in Israel falls through the cracks, and Paul insists God is not the author of confusion but of peace. Structure is not the enemy of the Spirit — it is one of the ways His care keeps arriving.
lens_gloss: inheritance, allotted portion — God's care arrives with names and order; provision is planned, not improvised.

note_title: Not shallow peace but holy fire.
note_body: Matthew hears Jesus speak of a sword and Luke hears Him speak of fire, and both refuse the same counterfeit: a peace that leaves falsehood undisturbed. The Spirit's gentleness is honest — it divides what is false from what can live.
lens_gloss: a short sword — truth's blade that divides false peace from true; it separates, it does not slaughter.

note_title: Astonishment is part of the witness.
note_body: Saul's old acquaintances cannot square the man they knew with the man now prophesying, and the council marvels at unlearned Peter and John before realizing they had been with Jesus. When the Spirit changes a person, other people's confusion is often the first evidence.
lens_gloss: to prophesy — Spirit-given speech breaking out where nobody expected it, surprising even the speaker's oldest acquaintances.

note_body: Samson counts his heaps and rhymes his own name into the victory, while the psalmist hands the glory straight back: not unto us, but unto thy name. Gratitude spoken first keeps a win from becoming a monument to self.
lens_gloss: jawbone — also the place-name Lehi; Samson's boast rhymes over the weapon until thirst teaches him the Giver.

note_title: A bowed ear is a humble ear.
note_body: The Spirit speaks to the one who has an ear, and Proverbs shows the posture: bow thine ear unto understanding. Hearing is not a talent — it is a bending, and the bending is the humility.
lens_gloss: to hear, to heed — the same verb covers sound reaching the ear and truth reaching the will.

note_body: Adam greets God's gift with glad recognition — bone of my bones — and Peter tells husbands to keep that spirit alive: giving honour, heirs together of the grace of life. What God hands us is received with gratitude, never gripped with fear.
lens_gloss: bone, essence — Hebrew's word for one's very self; Adam recognizes another self, equal in substance, given not grasped.

note_title: The robes are put on him.
note_body: Exodus commissions holy garments, and Leviticus shows Aaron standing still while Moses clothes him piece by piece. The servant does not dress himself for glory — identity for ministry is conferred, not performed.
lens_gloss: garment — clothing for service is issued, not styled; what covers the priest points past him to the holy purpose.

note_body: The Spirit rushes on Samson and the ropes fall away like burnt flax, and Hebrews files that moment under faith: out of weakness were made strong. What binds you is real — and it is still weaker than the Spirit of the Lord.
lens_gloss: to rush upon, to come mightily — the Spirit's sudden empowering that snaps what pressure had tied.

note_body: Jesus warns that endurance will cost the crowd's approval, and the risen Christ finishes the thought in His letter to Smyrna: be faithful unto death, and the crown — not the applause — is His to give.
lens_gloss: to remain under; endurance that stays at its post beneath the weight when no applause ever comes.

note_body: Generations later the psalmist retells this very scene — flesh rained down like dust — as a caution, because Israel got everything the craving demanded and still walked away unhealed.
lens_gloss: the quail — the craved meat that fell in heaps; proof that receiving what desire demands is not the same as being healed.

note_body: In Timnath the honey became a weapon turned against Samson; in the psalm God offers honey out of the rock Himself — a sweetness no schemer can plow up or use to corner you.
lens_gloss: a riddle, a dark saying — the hidden thing others tried to plow out of him rather than receive in trust.

note_body: The people shouted for Saul on his choosing day, and a later multitude shouted Hosanna for great David's greater Son — both crowds prove a coronation shout cannot keep a heart; only God's choosing holds when the noise dies down.
lens_gloss: to choose deliberately — Saul stood tall because the LORD chose him, not because the people shouted; choosing outlasts cheering.

note_body: The Spirit who put teaching in Bezaleel's heart is the same Spirit Paul describes giving to every man to profit withal — a gift is placed in one person precisely so it can reach many.
lens_gloss: to point, direct, instruct — the root beneath 'torah'; teaching as aiming another's hands toward God's own pattern.

note_body: Genesis names the river's course and the land that holds the gold, and Job agrees — there is a place for gold where they fine it; in God's world, precious things are located and bounded, never left to drift.
lens_gloss: to circle, encompass — the river runs free yet keeps its assigned circuit; liberty with a boundary and a name.

note_body: Judges watches the old evil return after rest, and Hosea names the ailment — a goodness like the morning cloud and early dew that goeth away; the Lord is after a surrender that outlives relief.
lens_gloss: to add, to do again — the quiet verb of relapse; the old evil rarely announces itself, it simply adds one more time.

note_body: When Moses buckled under the weight of the people, God said gather seventy; when the apostles buckled under the daily serving, the Spirit said look out seven — heaven's answer to a crushing load is shared, Spirit-filled shoulders.
lens_gloss: to gather in — God's first word to a depleted leader is a gathering word; the load was never meant for one set of shoulders.

note_title: The audit of the empty purse.
note_body: What Jesus commands here He later audits on the night He was betrayed — when I sent you without purse, lacked ye any thing? — and their answer, Nothing, is the testimony of every lean road He has ever assigned.
lens_gloss: to acquire, procure for oneself — Jesus forbids stockpiling security before obedience; courage travels on the Sender, not the savings.

note_body: In Gideon's day the camels without number came to strip the land; in Isaiah's vision a multitude of camels covers it again — this time bearing gold and incense and the praises of the LORD, the very image of overwhelm turned into worship.
lens_gloss: the locust swarm — Scripture's picture of pressure past counting; a multitude that has never once impressed the LORD.

note_body: What God assigns in Genesis, David turns into astonished worship in Psalm 8 — Thou madest him to have dominion — because stewardship carried rightly always bends back into praise, never into grasping.
lens_gloss: to rule, hold dominion — governance as caretaking under God's eye; authority that answers to the One who granted it.

note_title: They heard, and their feet answered.
note_body: Israel leaves Moses' presence and comes back with willing offerings, just as Hezekiah's people brought abundance as soon as the commandment came abroad — in both rooms, hearing turned into motion before the sermon cooled.
lens_gloss: to go out — leaving the meeting is part of the meeting; they carried the instruction out the door toward obedience.

note_title: The river and the island agree.
note_body: The blazing figure who dropped Daniel to the ground beside the Tigris meets John on Patmos with the same eyes of fire — and both men are raised from their faces with a fear not, because the Christ who overwhelms is the Christ who steadies.
lens_gloss: flame — eyes like a flame of fire; a gaze that burns through pretense not to destroy the beholder but to purify him.

note_body: The same words spoken over Othniel — the Spirit of the LORD came upon him — are promised to Saul with this addition: thou shalt be turned into another man; God's rescue begins inside the vessel before it changes the battlefield.
lens_gloss: breath, wind, Spirit — the empowering breath of God that comes upon a person for a task far too large for them.

note_body: Saul tells the plain truth about the donkeys and holds the kingdom in silence, doing exactly what Proverbs praises — a wise man keepeth it in till afterwards; restraint is not deceit, it is timing under God.
lens_gloss: to tell, declare — the verse uses it twice: Saul plainly declared the donkeys and left the kingdom undeclared; declaring less can be wisdom.

note_body: The evicted spirit wanders waterless country finding no rest, and Isaiah announces God's alternative landscape — water on the thirsty, floods on the dry ground, His Spirit poured out; a swept house must become a filled one.
lens_gloss: waterless — the parched country of a life merely vacated; only poured-out water keeps an emptiness from becoming an invitation.

note_body: Moses presses his hands onto Joshua at God's command, and Antioch fasts, prays, and lays hands on Barnabas and Saul — in both scenes the blessing is completed not by holding on but by sending away.
lens_gloss: to lean upon, lay with weight — commissioning presses real weight onto another; trust transferred through the hands, then released.

note_body: Genesis hangs the lights to serve the earth, and Psalm 136 tells you why in its refrain — He made great lights, for His mercy endureth for ever; every sunrise is mercy arriving on schedule, asking for thanks instead of striving.
lens_gloss: light-bearer, lamp — the same word used for the sanctuary lampstand; the great lights are servants set in place, not masters to chase.

note_title: Of thine own have we given.
note_body: The blue, purple, and scarlet of the tabernacle and David's heaped-up temple gold tell one story — all things come of Thee, and of Thine own have we given Thee; surrender does not lose a possession, it routes it home.
lens_gloss: the costly blue-violet of the sanctuary — ordinary wool made heaven-colored the moment it was set apart for God's dwelling.

note_body: Eglon's servants explained the locked doors wrongly, and David's men explained the cave wrongly too — people narrate what they can see, and freedom in the Spirit answers with patience instead of panic while the story is still incomplete.
lens_gloss: to bolt, lock — some doors stay barred for a season on purpose; the locked room is doing work the watchers cannot see.

note_body: Samson promises himself one more strike — I will be avenged, and after that I will cease — but revenge never keeps that schedule; Paul gives the ending grace writes: give place unto wrath, for Vengeance is mine, saith the Lord.
lens_gloss: to avenge — a word Scripture reserves chiefly for God; seized by human hands, it never ceases on the schedule we promise.

note_body: The wind that piled quail around a craving camp became the church's warning centuries on — these things were our examples, that we should not lust as they lusted; what God sends can test a heart as deeply as what He withholds.
lens_gloss: wind, breath, spirit — one Hebrew word for all three; the wind that carried the quail came from the same LORD whose breath fills the heart.

note_body: The lights appointed for signs and seasons in Genesis reappear in Jeremiah as covenant proof — the LORD who gives the sun by day and orders the moon and stars will not let go of His people; the calendar itself is a promise.
lens_gloss: appointed time, meeting — the word for God's festival appointments; the sky itself keeps a calendar of meetings with God.

note_body: These hard words are Micah's before they are Matthew's — the divided house, the daughter against her mother — and Micah shows where such a heart lands: therefore I will look unto the LORD, an allegiance that holds when the household strains.
lens_gloss: to cut in two, set at variance — Jesus does not deny the cut; He asks to be loved first, even through it.

note_body: God leaves nations in the land to prove a generation that had never known the wars, and Peter tells the church to think the fiery trial not strange — in both testaments the test is enrollment in strength, not evidence of rejection.
lens_gloss: to test, prove by trial — the proving that trains rather than shames; God tests to build what theory alone cannot carry.

note_title: Gathered to hear, sent to do.
note_body: Moses assembles the whole congregation around words the LORD commanded that ye should do them, and James presses the same charge on the church — be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only; listening completes itself in obedience.
lens_gloss: to assemble — the root of the called-out congregation; faith matures in the room where God's word is heard together.

note_body: Saul's uncle pressed him and Jeremiah's princes pressed harder, and both men answered honestly without surrendering what God had not released — the matter was not perceived, and it did not need to be, yet.
lens_gloss: to say — what the prophet said to you privately is not owed to every asker; some sayings must ripen in secret first.

note_body: Gideon's toppled altar set the whole town asking who did this, just as the healed man's carried bed set the rulers demanding what man told thee — obedience has always been interrogated before it is honored, and courage holds while the questions spread.
lens_gloss: to seek, inquire — the town spent its seeking hunting an obedient man; the same word Scripture uses for seeking the LORD.

note_title: Reverent feet at the right door.
note_body: The daughters stand at the tabernacle door with their hard case, and Deuteronomy names that very path — when a matter is too hard for the gates, carry it up to the place where God speaks. Courage and reverence can walk in together.
lens_gloss: to stand, to take one's stand — the posture of reverent petition; the daughters plant their feet before authority without shame.

note_title: The word that gathered still holds.
note_body: Peter looks back at the same gathering word — the earth standing out of the water because God said so. What His voice collects into place, His voice keeps standing.
lens_gloss: to be collected toward one place — kin to Hebrew's word for hope; what God gathers finds ground to stand on.

note_title: Zeal can aim at the obedient.
note_body: The men of the city call Gideon's obedience a capital offense, and Jesus warns His disciples the pattern will continue — some will harm you thinking they serve God. Knowing the cost ahead of time keeps obedience from turning bitter.
lens_gloss: to tear down, demolish — obedience sometimes looks like demolition before it looks like deliverance.

note_body: Matthew names the councils; Luke carries the same warning straight into comfort — when they bring you in, take no anxious thought over your answer, for words will be given. Accusation gets a room, but adoption gets the last say.
lens_gloss: to hand over — the very word used of Jesus' own betrayal; the disciple is handed into rooms the Father still governs.

note_title: The sevenfold Spirit before the throne.
note_body: Isaiah watched the Spirit rest on Messiah in fullness — wisdom, understanding, counsel, might — and John greets the churches from that same fullness burning before the throne. Grace and peace arrive carried by the whole Spirit of God.
lens_gloss: grace — favor that arrives as gift before anything is asked; the letter opens with supply, not demand.

note_body: Samson feasts because that is what young men did; Revelation blesses those who sit down because the Lamb has called them. One table sweeps a heart along, the other sets it apart.
lens_gloss: a feast, a drinking-banquet — celebration that can sweep a heart along with custom unless God sets it apart.

note_body: The tree of life planted in Eden's midst stands again in the city's midst, its leaves healing the nations. What desire once grasped at, grace will one day freely serve.
lens_gloss: life — Hebrew speaks it in the plural, a fullness of living; God plants abundance, not bare existence.

note_body: Joshua receives his commission before Eleazar and all the congregation, and Paul charges Timothy the same way — in the sight of God and of witnesses. Calling is safest where loving eyes can hold it accountable.
lens_gloss: to charge, to commission — a spoken entrusting that turns private calling into visible, accountable responsibility.

note_title: Spun in Sinai, sewn in Joppa.
note_body: The wise-hearted women bring what their own hands spun for the sanctuary, and centuries later widows hold up Dorcas's garments as her testimony. In both rooms, quiet needlework preaches what love had been doing all along.
lens_gloss: wise-hearted — wisdom seated in the heart and worked out through the hands; skill counted as a spiritual offering.

note_body: Gideon cries out because he has seen the angel of the LORD face to face; Jacob named a whole place Peniel for the same astonishment — I have seen God, and my life is preserved. Awe and mercy meet in the same gaze.
lens_gloss: face to face — nearness with nothing between; the presence that makes reverence tremble and mercy unmistakable.

note_body: The men listed in Matthew reappear in the upper room, temperaments intact, waiting together for the promise. The Spirit does not fall on interchangeable images but on real, unranked people gathered in one place.
lens_gloss: tax collector — a despised label kept in the apostolic list; calling is never embarrassed by a redeemed history.

note_title: Power learns from the meek One.
note_body: The Spirit rushes on Samson with lion-tearing strength, yet the Lord who carries the Spirit without measure calls Himself meek and lowly in heart. Strength is only safe in a heart still willing to learn.
lens_gloss: to rush upon with sudden power — the Spirit's strength can arrive before character has finished forming.

note_body: Before any rain or plowman, God waters the ground unseen; Hosea hears the same heart in a promise — I will be as the dew unto Israel. Quiet mercy comes first, and roots grow because of it.
lens_gloss: a mist rising from the ground — mercy that waters without thunder, preparing soil before any life appears.

note_body: Moses hears his ending spoken as being gathered to his people, just as Abraham heard he would go to his fathers in peace. God speaks of limits with the vocabulary of homecoming, not abandonment.
lens_gloss: to gather in, to bring home — death spoken as harvest and homecoming, never as being discarded.

note_title: Pray the coalition into God's hands.
note_body: In Judges the enemies band together and take the city of palms; in Psalm 83 the faithful take every banded name straight into prayer. Gathered pressure is answered by a gathered-up heart before God.
lens_gloss: to seize, take possession — pressure aims to occupy what belongs to God's people; naming the intrusion begins the resistance.

note_body: Samuel assembles Israel unto the LORD at Mizpeh, and in that same place Jephthah once uttered all his words before the LORD before leading anyone. Public moments stay steady when God hears everything first.
lens_gloss: to summon with a calling cry — the assembly is convened toward the LORD, not toward the crowd's opinion.

note_title: The willing mind still weighs most.
note_body: In the wilderness God receives whatever willing hearts bring — every man and woman together. Paul confirms the scale never changed: acceptance rests on the willing mind, not the size of the gift.
lens_gloss: a freewill offering — a gift moved by desire rather than demand; worship that volunteers.

note_title: Doors are allowed to stay shut.
note_body: Ehud locks the parlour and walks on without looking back, and Paul names that discipline for the soul — forgetting what is behind, reaching toward what is before. Some finished things are meant to stay finished.
lens_gloss: to shut, to close firmly — some assignments end with a door meant to stay closed behind you.

note_body: Isaiah told a threatened people not to catch the crowd's dread — let the LORD Himself be your fear. Jesus offers His disciples the same holy exchange: one right reverence quiets a thousand panics.
lens_gloss: to fear — the same verb forbidden toward men and commanded toward God; the question is never whether, but whom.

note_title: The burden becomes a shared law.
note_body: Moses tells God plainly that the weight of the people is too much for one servant. Paul writes God's remedy into the church's charter — bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
lens_gloss: a burden, a carried load — the word admits the weight is real; honesty about the load is where help begins.

note_body: Genesis shows the lights made with purpose; Isaiah bids you lift your eyes and take the roll call — He brings out their host by number, and not one faileth. A God that careful can carry your large concern.
lens_gloss: a light-bearer, a lamp set in place — light given an assignment; nothing God kindles is left to drift.

note_body: Moab's stout men of valour fall in a single day, and David's psalm tells why such strength never holds — enclosed in their own fat, they speak proudly. What intimidates is not what endures.
lens_gloss: stout, well-fed — strength that looks unbeatable; Scripture notes it chiefly to record its fall.

note_body: At the tabernacle dedication and at Gideon's rock, fire consumes only what has been fully laid down, and the people fall on their faces. What God accepts, He takes whole — and worship is the right response.
lens_gloss: to eat, to devour — the fire consumes the whole gift; what God accepts, He takes entirely.

note_body: The Spirit who filled Bezalel with wisdom for workmanship is the same Spirit Paul says distributes diversities of gifts today. Craft and calling flow from one Giver, so no gift has to perform.
lens_gloss: to fill full — the Spirit does not decorate a worker but fills one, until wisdom reaches the hands.

note_body: Israel journeys on from the Graves of Craving instead of settling there, and Isaiah carries the mercy forward — remember not the former things, for God is doing a new one. Corrected places become mile markers, not homes.
lens_gloss: to pull up stakes and set out — the corrected place becomes a mile marker, not an address.

note_body: Genesis shows every living thing called forward in order and given its place; Isaiah adds the tenderness — the Creator still gives breath to the people and spirit to them that walk on His earth. Your place in His care is not in question.
lens_gloss: living soul — life as a breathed, belonging thing; every creature has a place because God called it forth.

note_body: David sends peace to a house before he asks for anything; Jesus sends His disciples through the doors of Israel the same way. The greeting itself is ministry — peace offered before outcomes are known.
lens_gloss: to greet, to embrace with welcome — a doorway word; the disciple's first gift is blessing spoken before asking.

note_body: Judges records a grim scene without decorating it, and Habakkuk gives the fitting posture before heavy judgment — the LORD is in His holy temple; let all the earth keep silence. Sobriety, not spectacle, guards the witness.
lens_gloss: blade — the same word elsewhere means flame; Scripture records judgment's edge soberly, never as entertainment.

note_body: Saul, freshly anointed, absorbs contempt without a word; generations later the true Anointed stands accused and answers nothing. Men who know who God says they are can afford to hold their peace.
lens_gloss: to hold one's peace, to stay silent as though deaf — the anointed strength that refuses to answer contempt with self-defense.

note_body: The Philistines twist a marriage into leverage with threats of fire; Paul refuses enticing words altogether, because the Spirit's power persuades without a single threat.
lens_gloss: to entice, to lure with pressure — counterfeit persuasion that twists relationship into leverage, everything the Spirit's honest power never needs.

note_title: Two treasuries, the same open hands.
note_body: In Moses' day they brought dyed cloth and skins; in David's day, precious stones for the temple treasury. Different generations, one movement — whatever is found with you turns holy when it is handed over.
lens_gloss: to find, to be found — the offering begins with what is already discovered in your hand, not what you wish you had.

note_body: God spreads the Spirit resting on Moses across seventy shoulders so no one carries the people alone; Paul tells the church the same secret — many gifts, but the same Spirit.
lens_gloss: wind, breath, spirit — the one Spirit of God, generous enough to rest on seventy elders without leaving Moses any poorer.

note_body: Genesis closes creation week with everything complete; Hebrews reaches back to that seventh day to say the rest still stands open. You enter what God finished — you do not finish it yourself.
lens_gloss: to be finished, brought to completion — God's work stands whole, so your rest never depends on your striving.

note_title: Twenty years, and heaven's roll call.
note_body: Judges sums up Samson's turbulent life in one steady line; Hebrews reads that same life and writes his name among the faithful. The pattern God sees over a surrendered life is longer than its worst chapter.
lens_gloss: to judge, to govern and deliver — a calling measured in twenty years of pattern, not a single dramatic day.

note_title: A slandered household answers with light.
note_body: Jesus warns that His household will share the Master's slander; Peter shows the household how to answer — honest lives so plainly good that accusers end up glorifying God.
lens_gloss: master of the house — Jesus owns the household, so the names hurled at His family never get the final word.

note_body: Samson declares himself blameless before he strikes; Jacob's sons dress their vengeance for Dinah in covenant language. Twice Scripture shows how injury talks itself into innocence — so grace can interrupt the argument.
lens_gloss: to be clean, counted innocent — the word a wounded heart borrows when it wants revenge to feel righteous.

note_body: Genesis sets lights to govern and to separate; Jeremiah points to those same ordinances as proof of a covenant that cannot fail. The God who keeps day from night can keep your heart discerning.
lens_gloss: to separate, to make distinct — the merciful dividing that keeps darkness from ever passing itself off as light.

note_title: A mountain view, a finished race.
note_body: Moses climbs Abarim to see land another man will enter; Paul writes calmly with his departure at hand. Both bless work that continues without them, because the work was always God's.
lens_gloss: to see, to behold — God grants Moses sight of a promise his own hands will not finish, and calls it kindness.

note_body: Exodus shows offerings flowing from stirred hearts, not squeezed hands; Paul confirms the measure never changed — God receives the willing mind according to what it has, not what it lacks.
lens_gloss: to offer freely, to volunteer — the Spirit's stirring that turns giving from squeezed duty into willing joy.

note_body: Gideon's messengers travel tribe to tribe and the people come up to meet him; Hezekiah's letters ride the same roads calling a scattered nation home. God has always gathered His people by sent word.
lens_gloss: messenger, envoy — the same word as angel; ordinary carriers of a summons become holy when God does the sending.

note_body: Israel was commanded to love the LORD with all the heart; when Jesus asks for love above father and mother, He stands where that command stands — first love belongs to God, and He is claiming it.
lens_gloss: to love with tender family affection — Jesus does not despise this love; He asks to be loved above even this.

note_body: Judges counts five Philistine lords left to prove Israel; First Samuel counts them again, sending five golden offerings after God's hand humbled them. The pressures God names, God can also bring low.
lens_gloss: lord, ruler — Scripture's precise term reserved for Philistine lords; a pressure named and numbered is never vague.

note_body: In the wilderness, craving that rejected provision was named for what it was — despising the LORD who dwelt among them; Paul says the same of the Spirit-filled life: to despise it is to despise God Himself.
lens_gloss: to reject, to refuse as worthless — complaint's hidden verdict against the God who remains present in the camp.

note_body: Exodus 31 opens with God speaking before a single vessel exists; by Numbers, the ark, table, and candlestick that word called for are real enough to be somebody's sacred charge. Listening always comes before carrying.
lens_gloss: to speak — the covenant verb of initiative; before craft, calling, or assignment, God's own speaking sets everything in motion.

note_body: God sees the light, calls it good, and divides it from darkness; the Preacher measures by that same line — wisdom outshines folly as far as light outshines darkness. Discernment is agreeing with God's first verdict.
lens_gloss: good, pleasing, right — God names the light good before He divides; discernment begins by agreeing with His first verdict.

note_body: Numbers promised that when the trumpet sounded against an oppressor, God would remember and save; on Ephraim's mountain Ehud blows that very promise, and a people move because heaven is listening.
lens_gloss: ram's-horn trumpet — the summons that turns hidden deliverance into a people's public, faithful movement.

note_body: Saul answers his uncle's ordinary question with plain truth and lets the kingdom stay unspoken; Gehazi answers his master's question with a lie and loses everything. Ordinary doorways reveal what fire a heart is carrying.
lens_gloss: to walk, to go — the ordinary verb of daily errands, where a hidden anointing learns honest, humble speech.

note_title: The cry that learns to confess.
note_body: In Judges the people cry out because of Midian; by Samuel's day the cry has matured into confession — pressure named, sin named, mercy sought. God receives the first cry and patiently teaches it to become the second.
lens_gloss: to cry out in distress — prayer stripped to its honest bones, a named pressure carried straight to God.

note_body: Jesus authorizes leaving the city that refuses the witness; Acts shows what that leaving became — the scattered went everywhere preaching, and no closed door could keep the word from finding the next one.
lens_gloss: to flee — in Jesus' mouth not a coward's word but an obedient one; the witness moves on, it does not die.

note_body: Israel looked at heaven's daily provision and said 'nothing at all, beside this manna'; in John, Jesus lifts that same story to show what it always pointed to — God's true bread standing before dissatisfied eyes.
lens_gloss: manna — literally 'What is it?' — heaven's daily provision, so familiar that contempt learned to call it nothing.

note_title: A named river, a granted vision.
note_body: Genesis maps Eden's waters by name and direction; centuries on, Daniel stands beside that same Hiddekel and heaven speaks to him with precision. The God who gives rivers a course gives seekers one too.
lens_gloss: river — water with a name and a course; God's provision moves in directions that can be known and followed.

note_body: Sinai commands that the sabbath be kept holy; Luke shows women who loved Jesus keeping it still — spices prepared, grief waiting. Reverence for what God calls holy held even at their hardest hour.
lens_gloss: holiness, set-apartness — what God separates for Himself is handled with reverence, never as an ordinary preference.

note_body: Israel cried, and God's deliverer arrived left-handed — wrong by every expectation, right by God's design; Jeremiah names the pattern plainly: call on Me, and I will show you great things you do not know.
lens_gloss: bound or restricted in the right hand — Ehud's left-handedness; the very limitation God wove into Israel's deliverance.

note_title: The Guest who waits for the gift.
note_body: The angel tells Gideon, 'I will tarry until thou come again'; at Mamre the divine visitors likewise sit while Abraham hurries the meal. Heaven is never too rushed to wait on a willing, still-learning host.
lens_gloss: gift, tribute, offering — Gideon's small present laid before the LORD, hesitant faith's first concrete yes.

note_title: Hands laid where the Spirit lives.
note_body: Moses is told to lay his hand on a man in whom the Spirit already is; the apostles keep that same order — find those full of the Holy Ghost, then appoint. God prepares first; leaders only recognize.
lens_gloss: to lean upon, to lay hands — blessing's weight transferred; God's preparation recognized and made visible.

note_body: Sinai calls the sabbath a perpetual covenant observed through generations; Jeremiah shows exiles turning their faces toward Zion to join that everlasting bond again. A covenant kept in rhythm can always be rejoined.
lens_gloss: covenant, binding bond — kept in rhythm through generations, a promise practiced rather than merely admired.

note_title: Spoken in Eden, renewed in Christ.
note_body: Before Adam drew breath, God spoke the image; in Christ that same image is being renewed in you. What the Creator purposed at the beginning, the Spirit is still quietly forming — do not rush what He is restoring.
lens_gloss: image, likeness — God's stated purpose for humanity spoken aloud before any formed life was visible.

note_title: The task looked immovable; God wasn't.
note_body: Ehud walked toward an intimidating throne carrying an ordinary tribute, and Asaph learned the same secret in the sanctuary: what looks permanent can fall in a moment when God moves. Quiet courage does its duty and leaves the collapse to Him.
lens_gloss: a present, tribute, offering — the ordinary duty Ehud carried faithfully into an extraordinary assignment.

note_body: The word to Eli's house — them that honour me I will honour — becomes personal on the lips of Jesus: the mouth that owns Him before men is owned before the Father. Confession is not performance; it is honor answered with honor.
lens_gloss: to confess — literally to say the same thing; open agreement with Jesus spoken where people can hear it.

note_title: A hillside and an upper room.
note_body: The Spirit rushed on Saul among the prophets, and centuries later fell on a company in an upper room — both times, people who knew the old story had to reckon with new speech. When God's Spirit moves, He is not performing; He is remaking.
lens_gloss: to rush upon, come mightily — the Spirit's sudden overtaking that changes a man before his reputation can catch up.

note_title: Two cords, two chains, one purpose.
note_body: Samson was bound with two new cords and carried up from the rock; Paul was bound with two chains and carried toward Rome. In both stories the binding did not cancel the purpose — it became the road God used to reach it.
lens_gloss: to bind, tie — the cords that seem to hold a servant back often carry him into God's next act.

note_title: Daughters heard at the tabernacle door.
note_body: The Lord ruled that Zelophehad's daughters had spoken right and commanded their inheritance; Paul carries that verdict all the way home — in Christ Jesus, the inheritance passes over no one. God's justice does not run out at anyone's name.
lens_gloss: inheritance, allotted possession — the portion God Himself insists must not pass His daughters by.

note_title: Two young men, the same demand.
note_body: Shechem's get me this damsel and Samson's get her for me speak the same hurried language — eyes commanding, no one asking God. Scripture sets the two side by side so we will pause and ask which voice is shaping our wanting.
lens_gloss: to see — Samson's story runs on what his eyes report; desire grows dangerous where seeing goes unweighed.

note_title: The lamp made, the lamp kept.
note_body: Exodus names the pure candlestick among the crafted details, and Leviticus adds one quiet word: continually. God honors both the making and the daily tending that nobody applauds — the light stays lit because someone keeps ordering the lamps.
lens_gloss: lampstand — hand-worked detail whose whole purpose is keeping light burning before the LORD.

note_title: The first commandment was a yes.
note_body: Eden opens with lavish permission — every tree, freely — before any boundary is drawn, and Paul tells Timothy the same Father still gives every good thing to be received with thanksgiving. Obedience steadies when it remembers how generous God has already been.
lens_gloss: to eat — doubled in the Hebrew, eating you shall eat; God's first word to man is emphatic permission.

note_title: The God of Amen has a face.
note_body: Isaiah names Him the God of truth — in Hebrew, literally the God of Amen — and Revelation shows that Amen standing as a person, faithful and true before a single correction is spoken. The anchor for your waiting is not a mood; it is Him.
lens_gloss: so be it, firm, sure — a Hebrew word carried into Greek; Jesus wears certainty itself as a name.

note_body: Samson wins the battle and then cries out for water; Jesus finishes redemption itself saying, I thirst. God is not ashamed of a deliverer who admits need — honest thirst is where the strong finally pray.
lens_gloss: to thirst — the deliverer's own body preaching what his victories could not: he still needs God.

note_title: The same question, answered by God.
note_body: Moses asks where flesh could come from; the disciples ask where bread could come from in a wilderness — and in both stories it is God, not the weary leader, who furnishes the table. The question you cannot answer is His invitation to supply.
lens_gloss: flesh, meat — the need Moses cannot produce; naming the impossible out loud is where dependence begins.

note_body: Rebekah carried her bewilderment straight to the LORD and asked; Israel had to ask the LORD where their new king was hiding. God answers honest enquiry — even about the ones crouched among the stuff — so the cure for hiding is asking.
lens_gloss: to hide oneself — the same verb Adam used in the garden; fear's oldest reflex when the call comes near.

note_title: None did search — so He sent.
note_body: Ezekiel grieves sheep scattered on every mountain with no one seeking them; Jesus answers that old grief directly, sending the Twelve first to the lost sheep. Heaven's response to none did search is somebody sent.
lens_gloss: lost, perishing — not merely wandered but in danger of being destroyed; the word carries the urgency of compassion.

note_body: Judges records the cry and the deliverer God raised; generations later Nehemiah's people rehearse the same mercy — every time they cried, He heard from heaven and sent saviours. The pattern holds: stop coping, start calling.
lens_gloss: to cry out — not polite coping but a raised-voice appeal; in Judges, deliverance begins with this word.

note_title: Stakes that hold, stakes that stretch.
note_body: Exodus honors the pegs and cords that keep the sanctuary steady in the wind; Isaiah takes the same humble hardware and turns it into hope — strengthen thy stakes, because God intends to enlarge the tent. What anchors you now is preparing you for more.
lens_gloss: tent peg, pin — the small driven anchor that keeps the sacred structure standing when wind pulls at it.

note_body: Deuteronomy had warned of serving with no man to save; Judges counts eighteen honest years of it — and the very next verse begins deliverance the moment the people cry out. Long seasons are real, but they are not the last word.
lens_gloss: to serve, be bonded — the same word Israel used for Egypt; eighteen years under the wrong master, fully seen by God.

note_body: Genesis counts evening before morning — in God's reckoning the day opens with rest, not striving — and Jesus shows He knows every hour of the dark, naming even the cock crow before Peter's night unravels. Nothing your night holds is outside His knowledge.
lens_gloss: evening — the God-appointed close that opens the biblical day; rest comes first, and the work is His.

note_body: Joshua begs Moses to silence the surprising prophets; John reports forbidding a man casting out devils outside their circle — and both Moses and Jesus refuse the jealousy. God's work was never meant to fit inside our familiar company.
lens_gloss: to restrain, shut up — the reflex to close down what God never assigned us to stop.

note_body: God's design joins husband and wife in one-flesh cleaving, where secrets are safe; in Timnath, weeping becomes leverage and accusation crowds out trust. The contrast teaches tenderness that does not surrender truth.
lens_gloss: to weep — tears can be honest ache or applied pressure; discernment must hold both with a steady heart.

note_title: The prophet's grief, the Savior's honesty.
note_body: Micah lamented households turned against their own; Jesus takes up that very grief and stands inside it — the Lord who was Himself handed over does not ask you to carry family wounds He has not felt. Grieve honestly; obey anyway.
lens_gloss: to hand over, betray — the same word later used of Jesus Himself; He knows this pain from the inside.

note_body: Saul is told to wait seven days at Gilgal for a word he cannot supply himself; at Sinai the elders were told to tarry while Moses met with God. Obedience often looks like staying put under instruction until He comes.
lens_gloss: to wait, hope expectantly — the same verb the Psalms use for hoping in the LORD; tarrying is hope wearing work clothes.

note_title: The raided harvest has a promise.
note_body: In Judges, enemies come up and swallow what Israel plants; Isaiah answers with an oath sworn by God's own right hand — your grain will no more feed your enemies. Sow again under that oath, not under last year's loss.
lens_gloss: to sow — putting seed into ground you cannot guarantee; sowing is courage in slow motion.

note_body: Genesis shows the Spirit brooding over unformed waters before anything had a shape; the psalmist says that same Spirit still goes forth creating and renewing the face of the earth. The unformed places in your life are not abandoned — they are attended.
lens_gloss: to hover, brood — a mother-bird word; the Spirit stays over what is unformed until it is ready to live.

note_body: Moses speaks only what the LORD commanded, and Numbers shows the pattern continuing — offerings received and assigned to every man according to his service. When God's command orders the work, willing hands become worship instead of hustle.
lens_gloss: to command, appoint — the LORD's word giving shape to the work; waiting fills with purpose when His command arrives.

note_body: Numbers sets the rule — go out and come in at the LORD's word; Gibeon shows the cost when leaders examine the provisions but never ask at His mouth. The decision you are rushing deserves at least the pause the Urim required.
lens_gloss: lights — the priestly means of seeking God's judgment; decisions were meant to pass through light before they passed into action.

note_body: Gideon pleads his poor family and his own smallness in Manasseh; Paul calls himself less than the least of all saints — and in both lives, the smallness becomes the very platform where grace, not pedigree, does the saving.
lens_gloss: youngest, least — Gideon's own self-measurement; God's callings routinely begin below the family's expectations.

note_body: Seven days of pressing opened Samson's secret; Job's wife pressed him at his lowest and he held his integrity still. Endurance under pressure is decided before the seventh day — in the quiet resolve that relief is not worth the trade.
lens_gloss: to press hard, constrain — relentless pressure that outlasts resolve; the same word returns when Delilah presses him daily.

note_body: Genesis speaks light into darkness with a single word, and Paul says that same God has shined into our hearts. The word that opened creation is still His first gift to a soul waiting on the next step.
lens_gloss: light — spoken into being before sun or lamp existed; light that depends on God's word alone, not on circumstances lining up first.

note_body: Five sisters step forward by name and are received, not dismissed. Paul declares the same standing in Christ — neither male nor female — for God has always seen daughters as full heirs, not vague problems.
lens_gloss: to draw near — the worship word for approaching the altar; the daughters come near as worshipers with a real claim, not intruders.

note_title: The altar moves into the body.
note_body: Bezaleel crafted an altar where offerings were wholly given, and Paul calls the surrendered life itself a living sacrifice. Service stays warm when the whole self stays on the altar.
lens_gloss: altar — the appointed place of offering; holy work begins where something is truly given up, not merely performed.

note_body: Matthew states the cost of following, and Luke adds the word daily. Discipleship is not one heroic moment but a morning-by-morning yes to the same Lord.
lens_gloss: cross — the execution stake itself; not an ornament but a daily instrument of death to self-rule, carried while following.

note_body: Ehud calls the people forward because the LORD has already given the enemy into their hand, and David says the same in the valley — the battle is the LORD's. Guarding the ford is simply faith keeping what grace has given.
lens_gloss: to give — deliverance is spoken of as already handed over; obedience follows the gift, it does not earn it.

note_title: Another heart, then a new one.
note_body: Saul's story shows God turning a heart in a single moment, and Ezekiel promises the settled gift — a heart of flesh in place of stone. The Spirit's work always begins under the skin before it shows on the road.
lens_gloss: to turn, overturn, transform — God literally turned Saul another heart; real change is His inward turning before any outward sign.

note_title: A hidden blade, a living word.
note_body: Ehud girds a double-edged blade under his cloak long before he stands in the king's chamber. Hebrews names the true two-edged weapon — God's word, carried close, doing its deepest work where no one sees.
lens_gloss: sword — Ehud's blade literally has 'two mouths' (edges); preparation shaped in secret, ready for the decisive moment.

note_body: Genesis says God built the woman before He brought her, and the psalm says unless the LORD builds, the laborers work in vain. Help worth trusting carries His construction — receive it with gratitude, not suspicion.
lens_gloss: to build — the verb for houses and temples; God does not improvise provision, He builds it with intention before He brings it.

note_body: Numbers pauses to look again at the daily bread the people had stopped seeing, and Revelation promises hidden manna to the overcomer. God keeps feeding the eyes that keep noticing.
lens_gloss: manna — in Exodus 16:15 Israel named it from their own question, 'man hu,' What is it?; mercy stays a wonder only to hearts that keep asking instead of assuming.

note_title: A lampstand and a hillside city.
note_body: In the tabernacle the light needed prepared oil to keep burning, and Jesus calls His people the light of the world. Witness shines longest when the oil of hope is renewed underneath it.
lens_gloss: oil — the steady supply set apart for the light; lamps do not burn on their own resolve, and neither does witness.

note_body: Jesus warns that denial before men echoes in heaven, and Paul turns the same weight toward hope — those who endure shall reign with Him. The coming kingdom steadies today's confession.
lens_gloss: to deny, disown — to refuse to know someone publicly; loyalty is not a mood but a refusal to unname Jesus anywhere.

note_body: Moses said God led Israel forty years to prove what was in their heart, and Judges says the remaining nations served the same purpose. God's tests are never traps — they are mirrors held in mercy.
lens_gloss: to test, prove — not to trip the heart but to reveal it, so that obedience becomes owned rather than assumed.

note_body: John is in the Spirit on a prison island, and Ezekiel is carried in the Spirit into a valley of dry bones. The Spirit does His best-known work in the places nobody would choose.
lens_gloss: breath, wind, Spirit — one word for breathing and for Presence; exile could not thin the air of God around John.

note_body: Sinai fenced one day against the tyranny of output, and Hebrews says a sabbath-rest still remains for the people of God. The invitation to stop is not expired law but standing grace.
lens_gloss: sabbath, ceasing — the verse doubles it, 'shabbat shabbaton,' a complete stop; worth is received in the stopping, not earned in the striving.

note_body: Judges gives the land forty quiet years, and Nehemiah remembers how often rest was squandered into forgetting. Mercy's pause is meant for gratitude, not for sliding back.
lens_gloss: to grow quiet, be undisturbed — the settled stillness God gives a delivered land, and a delivered heart, after the struggle ends.

note_title: A table set for every breath.
note_body: Genesis shows God assigning food to everything that breathes, and the psalmist watches Him still growing grass for cattle and herb for man. Provision is not an emergency measure — it is His ongoing habit.
lens_gloss: living breath, soul — 'wherein there is life' is literally nephesh chayyah; every creature with breath is already on God's provision list.

note_body: The ruling won by five sisters becomes law for all Israel, and Paul says the comfort God gives us is issued for passing on. Your answered prayer is somebody else's map.
lens_gloss: inheritance, allotted portion — what God secures is meant to keep passing on; His provision never stops with one holder.

note_body: Gideon brings his trembling question to God and is not scolded for it. The psalm tells us why — as a father pities his children, the LORD pities them that fear Him; patience is part of His saving.
lens_gloss: to save, deliver — Gideon's 'if thou wilt save' uses the root behind the names Joshua and Jesus; salvation stays God's work even through trembling hands.

note_title: You name fear; He names you.
note_body: Jesus says hidden things will come to light, so fear need not govern the heart. Isaiah hears God answer fear with a name — thou art mine — and courage comes home as belonging.
lens_gloss: to fear, shrink back — Jesus does not shame the feeling; He removes its throne by promising nothing hidden stays hidden.

note_body: Israel brings silver, brass, and acacia wood as each hand finds it, and Paul says the willing mind is accepted according to what one has. God prices the release, not the amount.
lens_gloss: a lifted offering — a gift raised up off the pile called 'mine' and handed over into God's work with an open hand.

note_body: Scripture opens with a river leaving Eden to water the garden and closes with one flowing from the throne of God and the Lamb. The journey has always been resourced from the source, never from the road.
lens_gloss: river — supply that flows from a source before it divides toward its work; the garden drinks before it ever grows.

note_body: Moses obeys and sets Joshua before the priest and the people, and Deuteronomy records the fruit — Joshua full of the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid hands on him. One prompt obedience becomes the next generation's anointing.
lens_gloss: to command, charge — obedience here is simply doing the thing already said; no new revelation is required, only a willing yes.

note_body: The LORD steadies Gideon with peace before He ever sends him, and the risen Jesus does the same for Thomas behind locked doors. God's first gift to a frightened servant is Himself, spoken as peace.
lens_gloss: peace, wholeness — not the absence of Midian but the presence of God settling a shaking heart before any assignment begins.

note_body: Saul walks into music, prophecy, and a garrison's shadow all at once, and Numbers shows the same Spirit resting on seventy elders until they prophesied. When God's breath fills a place, His presence outweighs the pressure.
lens_gloss: to prophesy — to speak from the overflow of God's Spirit; an atmosphere charged by Presence rather than by performance.

note_body: God answers Gideon's weakness with 'Surely I will be with thee,' and the risen Jesus sends His church with the same word — lo, I am with you alway. Presence is still the whole provision.
lens_gloss: 'I will be' — the same verb inside God's own name at the bush; presence is who He is, not merely what He does.

note_body: Matthew's roll call names ordinary men — brothers, fishermen, a tax collector's neighbors — and Revelation shows those same names built into the foundations of the New Jerusalem. No name Jesus calls stays small.
lens_gloss: name — mission begins as a list of names; heaven's work is assigned to particular people, never to categories.

note_title: The outpouring goes home for supper.
note_body: Moses leaves the extraordinary moment and walks back into the camp, and the Spirit-filled church does likewise — breaking bread house to house with glad and single hearts. The outpouring is proven at ordinary tables.
lens_gloss: camp — the ordinary tents where the Spirit's gift must live among people; glory comes back to the neighborhood.

note_body: Genesis keeps time with a refrain — evening and morning, day after day — and Lamentations names what the rhythm carries: compassions new every morning. God's faithfulness is a repetition, not a rerun.
lens_gloss: morning — creation's returning refrain; every dawn is God repeating Himself in mercy for a heart that felt dry the night before.

note_body: Bezaleel's stone-setting and wood-carving were Spirit-filled work, and Paul says the same word over every task: do it heartily, as to the Lord. When detail is offered upward, repetition stops being drudgery and starts being devotion.
lens_gloss: Work of design — from the root for 'thoughts.' Skilled detail is thinking made visible, and offered to God it becomes devotion.

note_title: Moses warned it; Gideon lived it.
note_body: Deuteronomy foretold enemies who would leave no corn, wine, or oil, and Judges shows the stripped fields where it came true — yet the very next scene in Gideon's story is God calling a deliverer. The Word that named the emptiness had already planned the rescue.
lens_gloss: That which keeps alive, from chayah, 'to live' — the raiders stripped the means of living, but they could not touch the Giver of life.
